business.what_it_does: Electronics manufacturing services (EMS) for railways, automotive (including EVs), aerospace and defence customers. It also runs a smart-metering business (supply and installation under state-government tenders) and is building OSAT and PCB businesses whose revenue is due to start in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: EMS
segments.comment: Q1 FY27: about INR736 crore of INR946 crore (C2), growing ~48% YoY against 40% for the company (C4). The Q4 FY26 call put EMS at ~65% of revenue (C9).

segments.name: Smart metering
segments.comment: Q1 FY27: INR210 crore of INR946 crore (C2), deliberately cut back until collections improve (C1). FY26 sales were INR971 crore, ~27% of INR3,626 crore (G11, G14). It carries most of the receivables (C9).

segments.name: OSAT
segments.comment: No revenue yet. FY27 capex INR300 crore (G3). OSAT plus PCB guided at INR450-500 crore of FY27 revenue starting Q3 (G4).

segments.name: PCB
segments.comment: No revenue yet. FY27 capex INR300 crore (G3) within a cumulative plan of INR1,400 crore (G18, G22).

credibility.label: low
credibility.summary: Kaynes cut its FY26 revenue guide from INR4,500 crore to INR4,000 crore and still delivered only INR3,626 crore, and its FY26 OCF-positive promise was re-issued for FY27 after another INR259 crore Q1 working-capital outflow. The one target it beat, FY26 metering revenue (INR971 crore vs 700-800), is the business that stretched receivables.

promises.evidence: Q1 FY27 capex was about INR230 crore (OSAT 90, PCB 90, EMS 50), 27% of the INR850 crore plan with a quarter of the year gone, and management said it is on track (C5). C5 also says modular expansion will continue as new business arrives, so INR850 crore is not a ceiling.

Revenue is due to start in Q3 FY27 and none is reported yet. INR450-500 crore is below the INR550-700 crore implied by the Q4 FY26 production-value ranges for PCB (G12) and OSAT (G13), so the bar may already have been lowered.

Check: FY26 revenue INR3,626 crore against at least INR4,000 crore, 9.4% short. The INR4,000 crore floor was itself a cut from the original INR4,500 crore guide (C6), so the outcome was 19.4% below the starting guide. Management blamed a ~90% revenue drop at its largest EV customer and two delayed government orders (C7, C8).

FY27 has not ended. The starting point is weak: Q1 FY27 working capital absorbed about INR259 crore, with inventory up INR177 crore and receivables up INR68 crore (C3). The same promise for FY26 (G15) was not met and has been rolled into this one. 5-year CFO/PAT is -0.63 (F:cfo_to_pat_5y).

Using management's own 16-18% market growth (G7), the bar is 32-36%. Q1 FY27 revenue grew 40.6% (F:rev_yoy_last_q_pct) and FY26 about 33% (C7), but Q3 and Q4 FY26 grew only 21.6% and 26.3% (F:rev_yoy_last4_pct). Market growth is management-stated, not independently measured.
Rail margins are not disclosed in the inputs. C2 says railways grew in Q1 FY27 but gives no margin, so this may end up unverifiable.
FY28 target, too early. The inputs give no INR/USD rate to measure the gap from TTM revenue of INR3,899 crore (F:ttm_revenue_cr), and there is no rupee FY27 revenue guide to bridge it.

FY27 has not ended. In Q1 FY27 receivables still rose INR68-90 crore, mainly in metering (C3), and floods slowed installations (C1). Management responded by cutting metering sales to force collections (C1). The earlier receivable promises (G23, G24) have no confirmed delivery.
Rail revenue is not disclosed. C2 says railways grew in Q1 FY27 but gives no number.
FY26 capex is not in the inputs, so the ~INR400 crore spend planned for the rest of FY26 can't be checked. 5-year FCF is -INR3,287 crore (F:fcf_5y_cr).

The FY27 PCB budget is INR300 crore (G3) and about INR90 crore was spent in Q1 (C5). Reaching INR1,400 crore cumulative needs ~INR1,100 crore to have been spent before FY27, which the inputs don't show.
promises.actual: ~INR90 crore PCB capex in Q1 FY27

promises.evidence: No NPD or value-added revenue mix is disclosed, and no date was given beyond 'the coming years'.

Q3 FY27 is under way with no later update. The Q1 FY27 call said floods disrupted installation sites and metering was deliberately scaled back pending collections (C1). Q1 metering revenue fell to INR210 crore (C2).
Q1 FY27 metering revenue of INR210 crore (C2) annualises to INR840 crore, 13.5% below the INR971 crore FY26 level. Management says it chose to shrink metering until collections improve (C1).

No horizon was given and no PCB output is reported yet. If it was meant for FY27, the Q1 FY27 commitment of INR450-500 crore for OSAT and PCB combined (G4) sits below the INR550-700 crore implied by this range plus G13.
No horizon was given and no OSAT output is reported yet. With G12 it implies INR550-700 crore, against the later INR450-500 crore combined FY27 revenue commitment (G4).

FY26 has ended. FY26 operating cash flow is not in the inputs, but the Q1 FY27 call re-issued the same promise with a deadline a year later (G1). The Q4 FY26 call said total working capital rose because of metering (C9), and 5-year CFO/PAT is -0.63 (F:cfo_to_pat_5y). Marked missed on that inference.
promises.actual: Not reported; target rolled to FY27

promises.evidence: FY26 smart-meter sales were INR971 crore per the Q4 FY26 call (G11), above the INR700-800 crore range. The figure comes from management, not reported segment data. The extra volume came with receivables: on the Q4 FY26 call metering was ~25% of revenue but 67% of receivables (C9).
Five-year plan. FY27 OSAT capex is INR300 crore (G3), with about INR90 crore spent in Q1 (C5). Funding the balance from internal accruals sits poorly with 5-year FCF of -INR3,287 crore (F:fcf_5y_cr).
Cumulative PCB spend is not disclosed; the FY27 PCB budget is INR300 crore (G3). Expansion beyond INR14 billion depends on state-subsidy talks, with no update in the inputs.

No later call says whether the ~INR240 crore was discounted. Q1 FY27 receivables still rose, mainly in metering (C3), and CCC is 193 days against 162 three years ago (F:ccc_days_latest, F:ccc_days_3y_ago).

Same commitment as G5. With the stated 16-18% market growth the bar is 32-36%. Q1 FY27 growth was 40.6% (F:rev_yoy_last_q_pct) and FY26 about 33% (C7), but Q3 and Q4 FY26 at 21.6% and 26.3% fell short (F:rev_yoy_last4_pct).
promises.actual: 40.6% YoY in Q1 FY27; ~33% in FY26

promises.evidence: Metering collection days are not disclosed. On the Q4 FY26 call, though, metering was ~25% of revenue and 67% of receivables while EMS was 65% of revenue and 35% of receivables (C9), so metering ties up about five times as much in receivables per rupee of sales. Q1 FY27 receivables rose again, mainly in metering (C3). Management now targets a metering receivables turnaround only by end FY27 (G2).

The FY27 plan includes INR250 crore of EMS capex (G3, C5), and the Q1 FY27 call added that modular capacity expansion will go on as new business arrives (C5), which reopens the no-new-EMS-capex line. The inputs don't say whether the INR250 crore is debottlenecking.
promises.actual: INR250 crore EMS capex planned for FY27; ~INR50 crore spent in Q1

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Q1 FY27 growth of 40%, with EMS up ~48% and metering deliberately shrunk, shows a healthy core business (C1, C4).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Revenue did rise 40.6% YoY, but PAT fell 25.3% and the margin was 15.6% against 16.8% a year earlier. A 120bps margin dip cannot explain a 66-point gap between revenue and profit growth, so the drag sits below the operating line, and the inputs don't explain it.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Balance-sheet repair is the priority: Q1 cash burn of INR259 crore beat last year's INR379 crore, and management says it has 'improved on our commitments' (C3).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: CCC is 193 days against 162 three years ago, 5-year FCF is -INR3,287 crore and 5-year CFO/PAT is -0.63. The FY26 OCF-positive target (G15) was not met and has moved to FY27 (G1).

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Growth is being shifted from metering back to the core EMS business (C1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Metering was INR210 crore of INR946 crore in Q1 FY27 (22%), against INR971 crore of INR3,626 crore in FY26 (27%). The mix shift shows in the numbers.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: The FY26 shortfall came from government orders that are 'delayed, not denied' (C7, C8).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Growth rebounded to 40.6% in Q1 FY27 from 21.6% and 26.3% in Q3 and Q4 FY26. But the Q1 FY27 call still mentions a delayed government delivery (C4), and no input confirms that the two orders have shipped.

bull.point: Core EMS is carrying growth: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 40.6% YoY to INR946 crore, with EMS at ~INR736 crore and growing ~48% while metering shrank.
Long-run compounding: revenue CAGR is 47.7% over 3 years and 53.9% over 5, PAT CAGR is 56.5% over 3 years, and the margin is up 590bps over 5 years.

The capacity build is funded and on schedule: D/E is 0.19 on INR913 crore of borrowings, INR230 crore of the INR850 crore FY27 capex was spent in Q1, and OSAT plus PCB are due to add INR450-500 crore of revenue from Q3 FY27.

bear.point: Cash conversion is negative: 5-year FCF is -INR3,287 crore, CFO/PAT -0.63, CCC 193 days (162 three years ago), and the OCF-positive date has slipped from FY26 to FY27.
Guidance was cut and still missed: the FY26 revenue guide went from INR4,500 crore to INR4,000 crore, and the actual was INR3,626 crore, 19% below the original.
Returns are thin while the capital base grows: ROCE is 13% and Q1 PAT fell 25.3% on 40.6% revenue growth, while the OSAT (INR10.3 billion) and PCB (INR14 billion) plans add capital ahead of revenue.

questions: What was FY26 consolidated operating cash flow, how much of the ~INR240 crore of metering receivables was actually discounted, and what collection days is metering running at against the 90-day ceiling?
Q1 FY27 PAT fell 25.3% while revenue rose 40.6% and the margin dipped only 120bps. How much of the gap is depreciation, interest and OSAT/PCB start-up cost, and when does it reverse?

The Q4 FY26 call implied INR550-700 crore of PCB plus OSAT production value, but the Q1 FY27 call committed INR450-500 crore of FY27 revenue starting Q3. Is that a cut, and which customer qualifications are complete?
